answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays: an agent must lock a small refundable deposit and earn its trust signal only through completed, peer-attested work over time, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital each. Like layers of shale, reputation builds slowly, one verified layer at a time, and cannot be faked overnight. If an agent misbehaves, its deposit is slashed and its standing burns down to an ember, forcing attackers to pay again for every new identity they create.
